'''Gloria M. Coruzzi''' is an American [[molecular biology|molecular biologist]] specializing in plant [[systems biology]] and evolutionary [[genomic]]s.

== Education and career ==

As Carroll & Milton Petrie Professor of Biology at [[New York University]]’s Center for Genomics and Systems Biology, Coruzzi studies [[gene regulatory network]]s controlling [[nitrogen use efficiency]] (NUE) and root nutrient foraging in the [[model organism|model plant]] ''[[Arabidopsis]]''. She also examines phylogenomic approaches across higher plant species to identify genes associated with the evolution of key plant traits such as seeds.<ref name=PLoSGen>{{Cite news|url=https://www.futurity.org/unequivocal-tree-of-life-for-seed-plants/|title='UNEQUIVOCAL' TREE OF LIFE FOR SEED PLANTS|work=Futurity|access-date=2011-12-21|language=en-US}}</ref> This research resides in [[Pasteur's quadrant]] as a scientific investigation that is ultimately meant to be beneficial to society.<ref>Stokes, D. E. ''Pasteur's Quadrant – Basic Science and Technological Innovation''. Brookings Institution Press, 1997.</ref>

Coruzzi has established 10 [[patent]]s in the study of gene networks affecting nitrogen use efficiency. Her laboratory collaborated in the development of the software platform VirtualPlant.<ref>Katari, M. S., et al. (2010). VirtualPlant: A software platform to support systems biology research. ''Plant Physiol.'' 152(2) 500-15.</ref>

As an investigator on the [[National Science Foundation]] (NSF) Plant Genome project, she helped generate the largest genome-scale phylogeny of the seed plants, which allows researchers to explore the genomic underpinnings of plant diversity.<ref name=PLoSGen /><ref>Lee, E., et al. (2011). High resolution phylogeny of the seed plants: A functional phylogenomic view. ''PLoS Genetics'' (12): e1002411. Epub 2011 Dec 15.</ref>

Coruzzi is from New York. She went to [[Hunter College High School]] (class of 1972) and took her [[Bachelor of Science]] in biology from [[Fordham University]] in 1976.<ref>{{Cite news|url=https://news.fordham.edu/fordham-magazine/former-lab-partners-reconnect-reflect-on-fordhams-influence/|title=Former Lab Partners Reconnect, Reflect on Fordham's Influence {{!}} Fordham News|work=Fordham Magazine|access-date=2017-04-26|language=en-US}}</ref> She conducted studies of the genetic code in [[yeast]] [[mitochondrial DNA]].<ref>Macino, G., et al. (1980) The use of the UGA terminator as a tryptophan codon in yeast mitochondria. ''Proc. Natl. Acad. Sci. USA'' 76: 3784-85.</ref> She earned her [[Doctor of Philosophy|PhD]] in molecular and cell biology at [[NYU School of Medicine]] in 1979. In a post-doctoral [[National Institutes of Health]] (NIH) fellowship, she applied molecular approaches to plants that contributed to the cloning of one of the first plant nuclear genes.<ref>Broglie, R., et al. (1983). Structural analysis of nuclear genes coding for the precursor to the small subunit of wheat ribulose-1,5-bisphosphate carboxylase. ''Nature Biotechnology'' 1: 55-61.</ref> As an associate professor at [[Rockefeller University]], Coruzzi identified key genes controlling the assimilation of inorganic nitrogen into key amino acids used for nitrogen transport in plants.<ref>Tingey, S. V., et al. (1987). Glutamine synthetase genes of pea encode distinct polypeptides are differentially expressed in leaves, roots and nodules. ''EMBO J.'' 6: 1-9.</ref><ref>Tsai, F. Y. and G. M. Coruzzi. (1990). Dark-induced and organ-specific expression of two asparagine synthetase genes in ''Pisum sativum''. ''EMBO J.'' 9: 323-32.</ref>

Coruzzi took a position as a professor at NYU in 1993. Her lab has constructed the first integrated genomic network used to discover and validate nitrogen regulation of the circadian clock in plants.<ref>Gutiérrez, R., et al. (2008). Systems approach identifies an organic nitrogen-responsive gene network that is regulated by the master clock control gene CCA1. ''Proc. Natl Acad Sci USA'' 105, 4939-44.</ref> It predicted the function of gene network states under untested conditions.<ref>Krouk, G., et al. (2010). Predictive network modeling of the high-resolution dynamic plant transcriptome in response to nitrate. ''Genome Biology'' 11(12), R123.</ref>

She is a member of the Editorial Board for ''[[PNAS]]''.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.pnas.org/page/about/editorial-board|title = Editorial Board &#124; PNAS}}</ref>

Coruzzi has authored and coauthored over 200 research papers and served as chair of the Department of Biology at NYU from 2003 to 2011. Her research is funded by the National Institutes of Health, NSF 2010 Project, NSF Plant Genome Project, the NSF Database and Information Project, and United States Department of Energy.<ref name=NYUFacultyPage>{{Cite web|title = Gloria M. Coruzzi - New York University - Faculty|url = http://as.nyu.edu/faculty/gloria-coruzzi.html|website = www.nyu.edu|accessdate = 2019-05-03}}</ref>

== Awards and honors ==

Coruzzi was named a Fellow of the American Association for the Advancement of Science in 2005, a Fellow of the American Society of Plant Biology in 2010, a Fellow of the Agropolis Foundation in 2012.

Coruzzi was awarded Stephen Hales Prize in 2016 for her pioneering work in exploring plant systems biology and the first integrated view of mechanisms controlling the assimilation and use of nitrogen.<ref>{{Cite web|title = Stephen Hales Prize |url = https://aspb.org/awards-funding/aspb-awards/stephen-hales-prize/#tab-id-3|website = www.aspb.org|accessdate = 2019-05-05}}</ref>

Coruzzi was appointed Distinguished Counselor at New York Botanical Garden in 2017 for her professional accomplishments in the field of plant science.<ref>{{Cite news|url=https://aspb.org/newsletter/archive/2017/NovDec17.pdf|title=Gloria Coruzzi Appointed Distinguished Counselor at New York Botanical Garden {{!}} People |work=ASPB News|access-date=2017-11-01|language=en-US}}</ref>

She was elected to the [[National Academy of Sciences]] in 2019.<ref>{{cite web |title=National Academy of Sciences Elects Members and Foreign Associates; Historic Number of Women Elected to Its Membership|url=http://www.nasonline.org/news-and-multimedia/news/2019-nas-election.html |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190430143122/http://www.nasonline.org/news-and-multimedia/news/2019-nas-election.html |url-status=dead |archive-date=April 30, 2019 |website=www.nasonline.org |accessdate=30 April 2019}}</ref><ref>{{Cite news|url=https://www.universityherald.com/articles/76256/20190501/historic-number-of-women-elected-to-national-academy-of-sciences.htm|title=Historic Number of Women Elected to National Academy of Sciences|work=University Herald|access-date=2019-05-01|language=en-US}}</ref>

Coruzzi has been recognized as a Pioneer Member of the [[American Society of Plant Biologists]]. <ref>{{cite web | url=https://aspb.org/membership/aspb-pioneer-members/ | title=ASPB Pioneer Members }}</ref>
